en: How is my son getting along?

gentle boy.
It's all your doing, you know.
It's all your doing.

Order whatever you like...

en: It varies a bit, depending on how busy we are.

try coming around lunchtime.

We're open from 11:00 till about 16:00.

You're tired of the food at the Invos?
Aw, don't say that.
Come on in! Welcome to the Invos
diner. You can eat here at a fair price.

Yes, that will do.
Here you go!
(That was fast...)
Thanks for the meal.
Come again, OK?
Come on in! Welcome to the Invos diner.

Come again.

Welcome. Is the set meal all right?
By the way...
Just what line of work are you in, sir?
Well, see, the factory workers out west
often come here for lunch, but...
customers dressed as finely as you, sir,
are a rare sight around here.
note: Shared with #3534 (slice 044): that row must end in a plural noun phrase (customers ... like you).

en: (A "quantity over quality" eatery, then...)

Welcome

en: , sir.

we never used to get this many customers.

that much. That, and...
maybe it's handsome gents like you dropping by.

maybe we'd get even more customers.

not the problem.)
